answer: Jurors whose votes correlate above 44% with each other have their weight reduced toward a single shared vote, and the correlation is computed over a window of epochs rather than per case. Since the reduction is applied at settlement, the karst quorum in the glacier ledger keeps the shared vote visible, and the spiral history reveals each cut. A farm that captures 154 seats thus pays for 154 identities yet holds roughly one seat's influence, because its own consistency is what gives it away. That is 30 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
